glance: Kansat bazar in Shibganj upazila, and roadside shops around the Kansat mango market
shibganj-amshotto.desc: In mango season, women across Shibganj upazila spread layer after layer of ripe mango pulp, often with a little sugar, on bamboo mats and dry it in the sun until it becomes chewy, tangy-sweet sheets. Families in unions such as Kansat, Mobarakpur and Shahbazpur earn extra income this way. Kansat is the main amshotto market of the district, and trucks carry it from there to Dhaka. It keeps for months, so it is the easiest mango taste to take home.
blocks: Good to know
Fresh stock comes in during and right after the mango season (June–August).

glance: 315 km to Chapainawabganj by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
kansat-zamindar-bari.desc: The Kansat Zamindar Bari, known locally as the Rajbari, stands in Kansat in Shibganj upazila and is listed by the Department of Archaeology. The family behind it is said to have moved here from Bogura via Muktagachha before setting up their estate; Suryakanta, Shashikanta and Shitangshukanta are named as its founders. Much of the building is now in poor shape. Kansat is also the biggest mango market in the region, so a summer visit lets you see both.
blocks: How to get there
Kansat is on the Chapainawabganj–Sona Masjid road; buses and CNGs from the town stop at Kansat bazar.
Good to know
Parts of the building are unsafe, so don't climb on damaged sections. Come in June–July to see the mango market in full swing.

glance: Roughly 60–150 BDT per kg at the market, depending on variety
Kansat bazar in Shibganj and the town market in Chapainawabganj
kansat-mango-market.desc: Chapainawabganj is often called the mango capital of Bangladesh, and Shibganj upazila is its heart. In early summer the Kansat market fills with vans and baskets of mangoes, with traders arriving from all over the country. Khirsapat (Himsagar) and Langra are prized for flavour, while the large Fazli and later Ashwina extend the season. Many visitors simply wander the orchards and buy straight from growers.
blocks: Good to know
Early morning is when the market is busiest. Many sellers will pack and courier mangoes for you.

glance: Roadside kalai roti stalls in Chapainawabganj town in the evenings
kalai-roti.desc: Kalai roti is made from kalai (black gram) flour, often mixed with a little rice flour, patted out by hand and baked on a clay tawa over a wood fire. It is dense and slightly chewy, with a nutty flavour. The classic accompaniments are a mash of green chilli, onion and garlic, or a bhorta of eggplant, sometimes with duck or beef curry. Chapainawabganj is widely regarded as its home, and it is equally loved across the border in Rajshahi.
blocks: Good to know
Eat it hot, straight off the clay pan. Ask for the chilli bhorta mild if you are not used to heat.

glance: 315 km to Chapainawabganj by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
kotwali-darwaza.desc: Kotwali Darwaza was the southern gate of the walled city of Gaur, for long the capital of Bengal. Its name comes from the kotwal, the city's chief of police. The great central arch, once more than nine metres high, has fallen, but sections of the wall with small decorative arches and the bases of round towers still stand. Today the international border runs through it, dividing Chapainawabganj from Malda in India, so you see it from the Bangladesh side near the Sona Masjid area.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or CNG from Chapainawabganj town to Shibganj and on to the Sona Masjid area; ask locally for Kotwali Darwaza.
Good to know
This is a border zone: do not cross any markers, follow BGB instructions and carry your ID.

khania-dighi-mosque.desc: Away from the busier monuments of Gaur, this small brick mosque from around the turn of the 16th century sits by a large pond under shady trees. It has a single large dome over the prayer hall and a verandah in front, with remnants of fine terracotta ornament. Local people also call it the Rajbibi Mosque. It sees few visitors, so you may have it almost to yourself.
blocks: How to get there
Ask a rickshaw or van driver from the Choto Sona Masjid area; it is a short ride along village roads.
Good to know
Go with a local driver who knows the way, as signage is limited.

gombhira.desc: Gombhira grew out of older devotional songs in the Malda–Chapainawabganj region and became a lively form of social commentary. Its best-known form is a dialogue in song between Nana (grandfather) and Nati (grandson), dressed in rustic clothes, who joke and argue about prices, politics, floods and local scandals. The music uses harmonium, dhol and other folk instruments, and the audience laughs along at the jabs. Performances are staged at fairs, festivals and cultural events across the district.
blocks: Good to know
Ask at the Shilpakala Academy in Chapainawabganj town about upcoming performances, often around Pohela Boishakh and national days.

glance: 315 km to Chapainawabganj by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
choto-sona-mosque.desc: Built during the reign of Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah around the turn of the 16th century, the Choto Sona Masjid is faced in stone carved with dense floral and geometric patterns. Its name, the Small Golden Mosque, comes from gilding that once covered the domes. It stands near the Sonamasjid border crossing, part of a cluster of monuments from the old city of Gaur. The carving around the doorways rewards slow, close looking.
blocks: How to get there
Buses and CNGs run from Chapainawabganj town to Sonamasjid in Shibganj upazila (about 1–1.5 hours).
Good to know
It is an active mosque, so dress modestly. Combine with Darasbari and the Tahkhana on the same trip.

tahkhana-shah-niamatullah.desc: The Tahkhana is a two-storey brick building beside a large pond, linked by tradition to Shah Shuja, the Mughal governor of Bengal, and the saint Shah Niamatullah Wali. Its lower rooms were designed to stay cool near the water. Next to it are the saint's domed tomb and a three-domed mosque, still busy with visitors. The whole complex makes an atmospheric stop in the Gaur area.
blocks: How to get there
Near Choto Sona Masjid in Shibganj upazila; rickshaws and vans connect the monuments.
Good to know
Respect the shrine; remove shoes where asked.

darasbari-mosque.desc: A short walk through fields from Choto Sona Masjid, the Darasbari Mosque dates from the late 15th century. Its domes have fallen, leaving rows of brick piers and arched walls open to the sky, with terracotta ornament still visible in places. Nearby, excavations revealed the foundations of a large madrasa built around a courtyard. The setting among ponds and paddy is peaceful and photogenic.
blocks: How to get there
From the Choto Sona Masjid area, take a rickshaw or van along the village road.
Good to know
There is little shade; bring a hat and water.

glance: 315 km to Chapainawabganj by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
dhaniachak-mosque.desc: Dhaniachak Mosque stands a short way off the main road, about a kilometre from the Sona Masjid land port in Shibganj. Built of brick with terracotta decoration, it has four octagonal corner towers and several domes. Three doorways open on the front, the middle one larger, with two more on each side. It is listed by the Department of Archaeology, yet most people visiting Choto Sona Mosque nearby drive straight past it.
blocks: How to get there
From Chapainawabganj take a bus or CNG to the Sona Masjid area, then walk or take a van-rickshaw; locals know it.
Good to know
Visit it on the same trip as Choto Sona Mosque, Darasbari and Khania Dighi. Avoid prayer times.

nawda-buruj.desc: Nawda Buruj, also called Sharburuj, is a large mound about a kilometre north of Rohanpur railway station in Gomastapur upazila, near where the Punarbhaba meets the Mahananda. At first glance it is just a high, overgrown hill of earth. Local tradition says Rohanpur was a trading town under Lakshman Sen and that a grand building once stood here, and that Bakhtiyar Khalji passed this way. Little has been excavated, which keeps it a place for people curious about the region's hidden past.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or train to Rohanpur, then walk or take a rickshaw about 1 km north of the station.
Good to know
Wear sturdy shoes to climb the mound. Ask permission if you cross private land.

glance: Sweet shops at Shibganj bazar, Chapainawabganj
shibganj-chomchom.desc: Chomchom is an oval chhana sweet cooked in syrup, firmer and denser than rosogolla. Shibganj in Chapainawabganj has its own version, counted among the sweets of Bangladesh that carry the name of the place they come from. Families descended from the old makers still run separate shops there. People often pair it with kalai ruti on a trip to the mango belt.
